title: More than one condition: AND and OR
summary: Check several conditions at once with AND, or at least one condition with OR.
intro:
`AND` returns `TRUE` if every condition is met, and `OR` returns `TRUE` if at least one condition is met. You write the conditions inside the function, separated by commas.

They help with decisions such as: does the applicant have enough experience and speak English? Or: do they live in a given city or have long experience?

faq.a: `FALSE`, because `AND` needs every condition to be true.

faq.q: How many conditions can I put in `OR`?
faq.a: More than two as well, separated by commas, and one true condition is enough.

and-worked-example.prompt: These people applied for a job. `AND` returns `TRUE` if every condition is met. In `E2`, type the formula `=AND(B2>=2,C2)` to find out whether Khaled has at least two years of experience and speaks English.

and-second-applicant.prompt: In `E3`, type the same formula for Mona.

or-worked-example.prompt: `OR` returns `TRUE` if at least one condition is met. In `F2`, type the formula `=OR(D2="Irbid",B2>=4)`: is Khaled from Irbid or does he have 4 or more years of experience?

or-second-applicant.prompt: In `F3`, write a formula that returns `TRUE` if Mona is from Irbid or has 4 or more years of experience.
